previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including sclerosing mesenteritis, chronic TPN dependence via a femoral catheter, and chronic pain was admitted for dizziness and low urine output due to dehydration. Her hypotension was attributed to missed home IV fluids due to insurance issues and fasting in preparation for a procedure. She received aggressive IV hydration, which stabilized her blood pressure. Due to persistent pain and irritation at the tunnel site of her femoral catheter, she underwent a successful re-tunneling procedure with imaging guidance. Her chronic pain remained poorly controlled on current opioid therapy, and she expressed concerns about escalating doses without benefit. Psychiatry and social work addressed her worsening depression related to recurrent hospitalizations. She was discharged home with stable vital signs, instructions to resume home care, and follow-up plans with her pain management, GI, and mental health providers.

Brief Hospital Course:
Assessment and Plan: ___ yo F with h/o mesenteric sclerosis in 
evaluation for intestinal transplant in ___ who presents with 
baseline abdominal pain but 3 days of chills.  
 
Active Issues: 
# Central line associated Pseudomonas bacteremia: Patient 
admitted ___ with fever and chills with ___ blood 
culture which grew pseudomonas sensitive to cefepime and 
levofloxacin. She intially had her right fem line removed (___) 
and new left fem line placed (___) which was kept sterile with 
ethanol locks. All blood cultures since admission were no growth 
final. Given the insurance difficulties with TPN and line care 
as outlined below, her line was removed by ___ prior to 
discharge. She completed a course of levofloxacin for 
Pseudomonal bacteremia prior to discharge.
 
# TPN/Nutrition: Patient previously on home TPN but insurance 
found out was taking PO. Therefore, will no longer pay for TPN.  
Most of her hospitalization centered around her dispo which 
proved to be exceptionally challenging. This mostly centered 
around payment for her home IV antibiotics and her home TPN 
which it was realized during this admission she will no longer 
qualify for since she is regularly taking PO. We are held her 
TPN and monitored caloric intake while she completed her course 
of IV antibiotics.  Nutrition assessement determined that the 
patient was taking adequate PO such that she no longer medically 
required TPN. As a result, her femoral line was removed prior to 
discharge.  Patient was encouraged to continue drinking Ensure 
Enlive supplements as well as regular diet as tolerated. 
 
#Sleepiness/Unstable gait: Very likely due to oversedation or 
delirium as completely normal neurological examination in the 
setting of multiple sedating medications. Patient rapidly 
improved. We held several of her meds including her ativan and 
gabapentin. Given rapid improvement, patient was restarted on 
ativan with meals to help with nausea and she had no further 
events of altered mental status.

# Sclerosing mesenteritis: Chronic and with multiple surgeries 
now being evaluated for intestinal transplant in ___. 
Needs to taper her narcotics before she can get full pre-op 
work-up for the transplant. She admits there is a component of 
IBS and anxiety in her pain and GI symptoms as well.  Patient 
was continued on her home morphine PR, bowel regimen, 
octreotide, misoprostol. For antiemetics, she was managed with 
IV ativan and phenergan.  Prior to discharge she trialed back on 
her home regimen (PR phenergan, no ativan) and she tolerated 
this well. 

# Vitamin D Deficiency / Calcium deficiency: Patient seen by 
endocrine. Patient was started on vitamin D3, calcitriol and 
calcium carbonate.  She was discharged on these medications and 
with endocrine follow-up.

# Depression/Anxiety:  Psychiatry consulted as well as patient 
had expressed passive suicidality. Also complained of 
pseudoseizures at times and occasional episodes of chest pain 
which have consistently been without EKG changes and with 
tenderness to palpation. Psych uncovered no active issues and we 
continued her home aripiprazole, trazodone and lorazepam.

Chronic issues:
# Migraines: Continued home topamax and supatriptan SC  

# h/o recurrent DVT: continued enoxaparin for prophylaxis; 
patient takes this at home.

# Hypothyroidism: Continued home levothyroxine

-Patient had difficulty believing she was taking in good PO and

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Rule out kidney stones in a ___ woman with flank pain.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:  AP supine views of the abdomen and pelvis, prominent gas-filled
loops of small and large bowel are seen in this supine view.  No definitive
radiodensities within the expected region of the kidneys or course of the
ureters to suggest kidney stones.  Single supine radiograph limits evaluation
for free air or air-fluid levels.  Surgical clips are noted over the spine and
the right upper quadrant.

IMPRESSION: 
Prominently distended loops of small and large bowel are compatible with
ileus.  No radiopaque kidney stones identified.

PROCEDURE:  GASTRIC TUBE REPLACED.

INDICATION:

___ female with longstanding gastric tube which was displaced
yesterday and a Foley catheter was replaced in its tract.  Today, the patient
comes in for repositioning of a new G-tube.

CLINICIANS:  Dr. ___ and Dr. ___, who was present
and supervising throughout.

ANESTHESIA:

Moderate sedation was provided by administering divided doses for a total of
75 mcg of fentanyl and 1 mg of Versed during which patient's hemodynamic
parameters were continuously monitored.  Local anesthesia was provided with 1%
lidocaine gel.

PROCEDURE AND FINDINGS:

A written informed consent was obtained after explaining risks, benefits and
alternatives to the procedure.  The patient was brought to the angiography
suite and placed supine on the imaging table.  The upper abdomen was prepped
and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  A preprocedure timeout was performed
as per ___ protocol.

A scout image of the abdomen was obtained and stored.  Small amount of
contrast was injected through the present Foley catheter, which demonstrated
intragastric position.  A ___ wire was advanced and coiled within the
stomach.  Subsequently, the Foley balloon was deflated and the tube was
retrieved.  Then, a 12 ___ ___ G-tube was placed over the ___
wire.  The wire was removed and retaining loop of the catheter was formed in
the stomach and locked after confirming the position of the catheter by
contrast injection.  The catheter was flushed, capped and secured to the skin
with a StatLock device.  Sterile dressings were applied.  The patient
tolerated the procedure well and there were no immediate complications.

IMPRESSION:

Uncomplicated exchange of a 12 ___ G-tube under fluoroscopic
guidance.

INDICATION:  ___ with left calf swelling, assess for DVT.

COMPARISONS:  ___.

FINDINGS:  Gray-scale and color Doppler sonographic evaluation was performed
of the left lower extremity.  Normal compressibility and flow is seen in the
left common femoral, paired superficial femoral, popliteal, peroneal, and
posterior tibial veins without evidence of DVT.

IMPRESSION:  No left lower extremity DVT.

CHEST RADIOGRAPH

INDICATION:  Cough, rule out pneumonia.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:  As compared to the previous radiograph, there is no relevant
change.  Normal lung volumes.  No acute changes.  Borderline diameter of the
azygos vein.  Spinal stimulator devices in situ.  Normal size of the cardiac
silhouette.  No evidence of pneumonia.

PROCEDURE:  Tunneled central line placement.

MEDICAL HISTORY:
___ female with history of TPN requirement, with a right tunneled
femoral line being removed three days ago, requiring a new line.  A request
was placed for a left femoral line placement.

CLINICIANS:
Dr. ___, ___ fellow and Dr. ___, ___ attending, was
present and supervised throughout the whole procedure.

ANESTHESIA:
Moderate conscious sedation was provided by administering divided doses for a
total of 100 mcg of fentanyl and 2 mg of Versed for this 35 intraservice time.
During this time, patient's hemodynamic parameters were continuously
monitored.

Local anesthesia was provided by using 1% lidocaine and 1% lidocaine with
epinephrine into the dermis and subcutaneous tissues.

PROCEDURE:
Written informed consent was obtained from patient after explaining risks,
benefits and alternatives to the procedure.

The patient was brought to the angiography suite and placed supine on the
imaging table.  The left groin was prepped and draped in the usual sterile
fashion.  A preprocedure timeout was performed as per ___ protocol.

After anesthetizing the skin and subcutaneous tissues, a micropuncture needle
was inserted into the left femoral vein under ultrasound guidance.  The hard
copy ultrasound images were saved for reference.  A 0.018 nitinol wire was
advanced into the inferior vena cava.  Subsequently, a small ___ was made in
the skin and micropuncture needle was exchanged with a micropuncture sheath. 
The inner cannula and nitinol wire were removed.  A 0.035 J-wire was advanced
into the cavoatrial junction.  Appropriate measurements were made from the
skin incision four fingerbreadths below the venotomy site.

Subsequently, attention was turned to tunnel creation.  After additional local
anesthesia, a tiny skin incision was made.  A 10 ___ tunneled catheter was
passed from the incision to the venotomy site, with aid of a tunneled metal
tunneling device.  The venotomy tract was dilated with the peel-away sheath. 
The wire and inner cannula were removed, and the catheter was passed through
the peel-away sheath.  The peel-away sheath was removed while the catheter was
pushed into the cavoatrial junction.  This was confirmed by fluoroscopy
demonstrating catheter tip in the cavoatrial junction.  Both lumens withdrew
blood and flushed easily.  Catheter was secured with ___ sutures.  Venotomy
site was closed with ___ Vicryl subcuticular stitches.  Dry sterile dressings
were applied.  No immediate post-procedure complications ensued.  The patient
tolerated the procedure well.

IMPRESSION:

Successful placement of a tunneled catheter line through the left femoral vein
approach.  The tip is in the cavoatrial junction and the catheter is ready to
use.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with tunneled femoral line, no longer
indicated, please remove.

PHYSICIANS:  Dr. ___ (radiology fellow) and Dr. ___
___ (radiology attending) who was present and supervised the procedure.

PROCEDURE DETAILS:

A preprocedure timeout was performed using three patient identifiers.  The
skin of the left groin was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion
including the existing tunneled femoral line.  Both lumens were aspirated;
removal of 10 cc of bloody fluid.  The suture was cut.  Approximately 3 cc of
1% lidocaine was infiltrated into the skin and subcutaneous tissues for local
anesthesia.  The catheter was removed without difficulty and firm manual
compression was applied at the femoral venotomy site for 10 minutes. 
Following completion of this maneuver there was no evidence of bleeding.  A
sterile dressing was applied to the skin incision.  There were no immediate
post-procedure complications.

IMPRESSION:  Successful removal of a tunneled left femoral line.
